$comment: Issue #17: the moons shown by default, curated by story, not by size. A moon is listed here when it has a story a student can repeat (the reason is the one-line pitch; the full story is in src/locales/<locale>/bodies.json, which must carry authored content for every moon listed here). Every other moon is the long tail: hidden until the viewer asks for all moons. Keyed by planet id, then moon id; the build fails on an unknown id or a wrong planet. The rule is written down in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, 'Moons'.

earth.moon: Our companion: phases, tides, eclipses, and the only other world people have walked on

mars.phobos: Spirals toward Mars and will be torn apart; rises in the west twice a day
mars.deimos: A speck of a moon that looks like a bright star from Mars

jupiter.io: The most volcanic world known, squeezed hot by Jupiter's tides
jupiter.europa: An ocean of liquid water under the ice: a place to look for life
jupiter.ganymede: The largest moon, bigger than Mercury, with its own magnetic field
jupiter.callisto: The most cratered surface known, unchanged for four billion years

saturn.mimas: The 'Death Star' moon with one giant crater
saturn.enceladus: Geysers of water shoot from an ocean under its south pole
saturn.tethys: A ball of almost pure ice with a canyon most of the way around it
saturn.dione: Bright ice cliffs, and two tiny moons sharing its orbit
saturn.rhea: Saturn's second-largest moon, with a whiff of oxygen
saturn.titan: The only moon with thick air, plus methane rain, rivers and seas
saturn.hyperion: A sponge-like moon that tumbles chaotically
saturn.iapetus: Two-faced: one side dark as coal, the other bright as snow
saturn.phoebe: Orbits backwards, a captured wanderer that paints Iapetus dark

uranus.miranda: A patchwork moon with some of the tallest cliffs known
uranus.ariel: The brightest, youngest surface of Uranus's big moons
uranus.umbriel: The darkest of Uranus's big moons, with a mysterious bright ring
uranus.titania: Uranus's largest moon, named after Shakespeare's fairy queen
uranus.oberon: The outermost big moon of the system tipped on its side

neptune.triton: Orbits the wrong way: a captured world with nitrogen geysers
neptune.nereid: One of the most stretched orbits of any moon
neptune.proteus: As big as a lump can get before gravity pulls it round

pluto.charon: So big that Pluto and Charon circle a point between them, each always showing the other the same face (#23)
